paras: Dopasia ludovici, also known commonly as Ludovic's glass lizard, is a species of lizard in the subfamily Anguinae of the family Anguidae. The species is native to Southeast Asia.
The specific name, ludovici (meaning "of Louis" in Latin), is in honor of French zoologist Léon Louis Vaillant.
Dopasia ludovici is found in northern Vietnam, and it has been reported to also occur in Sichuan, China.
Dopasia ludovici has no legs. Its dorsal scales are strongly keeled. It may attain a snout-to-vent length (SVL) of 19.5 cm (7.7 in).
The preferred natural habitat of Dopasia ludovici is forest, at altitudes of 1,000–1,500 m (3,300–4,900 ft).
Dopasia ludovici is terrestrial and fossorial.
